fictional_only.title: For fiction, games, and RPGs only
fictional_only.disclaimer: Every name, symbol, and territory this tool produces is invented fiction for stories and campaigns. It never reproduces real gang names, symbols, or identities, and it is not a directory of real-world groups.

items.title: Everything here is invented
items.description: The generator refuses real gang names, symbols, colors, hand signs, and structures on purpose. If a result ever echoes something real, discard it and regenerate.

items.title: Keep it clearly fictional
items.description: Give the group fictional members, a fictional city, and fictional stakes. Fiction-first framing keeps the story usable across publishers and platforms.

items.title: Avoid real-world harm
items.description: Don't adapt results to impersonate an active group, and don't use them for recruitment, intimidation, or anything aimed at real people or places.

items.title: Check before you publish
items.description: Before publishing, search the name in quotes. If it collides with a real organization or an established franchise, change a word or regenerate.

feature1.name: feature_intro
feature1.label: Styles
feature1.title: Choose a Style for Your Fictional Gang
feature1.description: Each world in the Gang Name Generator has its own naming logic. Pick a setting above, or scan the styles below to see how the conventions differ.

items.title: Crime noir & street crews
items.description: Modern crews take a place or a mark and wear it down: think 'the Dockside Nine' or 'the Halden Crew'. Short, local, and believable enough that locals would actually say them.

items.title: Mafia & mob families
items.description: Mob names lean on dynasty and respect: 'the Vermillion Court' or 'the Corvino Family' sound old, moneyed, and bound by oaths. Family surnames and honorifics do the heavy lifting.

items.title: Fantasy factions
items.description: Fantasy organizations pair an image with a vow: 'the Ashen Vow' or 'the Gilded Raven Company' promise magic, ruins, and mercenary history in three words.

items.title: Cyberpunk collectives
items.description: Neon crews splice tech slang with cult gravity: 'Static Zero Collective' or 'the Neon Synod' read like netrunner cells with a manifesto and a logo made of light.

items.title: Outlaw biker clubs
items.description: Biker names are chrome and scripture: 'Iron Halo Riders' or 'the Cinder Saints' pair metal with sanctity, the way riding clubs name themselves in fiction.

items.title: Funny gang names
items.description: Comedy gangs undercut the menace: 'Grandma's Alibi' or 'the Polite Ruckus' get a laugh and still hold a turf. Set the tone dial to Funny to generate in this register.

how_to_use.name: how_to_use
how_to_use.label: HOW TO USE
how_to_use.title: How to Make a Memorable Fictional Gang Name with the Gang Name Generator
how_to_use.description: Three steps with the Gang Name Generator from blank page to a name your characters can say out loud.

items.title: Establish world and tone
items.description: A mafia family and a cyberpunk collective should not share a vocabulary. Set the world, group type, and tone first in the Gang Name Generator — the name should be unthinkable outside its setting.

items.title: Combine image, value, and group type
items.description: Take a striking image (raven, ember, harbor), the code the group lives by, and its form — crew, clan, syndicate. 'Ashen' + vow + brotherhood gives you 'the Ashen Vow'.

items.title: Test the name in dialogue
items.description: Say it as a threat, a whisper, and a badge: 'Nobody crosses the Dockside Nine.' If it works in all three lines, it works on the page.

feature2.name: feature_benefits
feature2.label: Examples
feature2.title: Gang Names with Meanings from the Gang Name Generator
feature2.description: A taste of the profile format every generation returns — every name arrives with the story context around it.

items.title: The Vermillion Court — mafia family
items.description: Meaning: 'Vermillion' dresses old violence in aristocratic red, while 'Court' claims the family holds power like a dynasty. Reputation: untouchable at galas, feared at the docks. Use it when your story needs a family that has been ruling one city for generations.

items.title: Static Zero Collective — cyberpunk cell
items.description: Meaning: 'Static' is the noise they hide in, 'Zero' the footprint they leave; 'Collective' signals a manifesto, not a boss. Reputation: ghosts who claim credit with a signature glitch. Use it for netrunners who fight a corporation from inside its own network.

items.title: The Ashen Vow — fantasy brotherhood
items.description: Meaning: 'Ashen' carries a burned homeland and survivors' grief; 'Vow' makes the name an oath each member renews. Reputation: hired blades who keep contracts even kings break. Use it for a mercenary order with one unbreakable rule.

items.title: How do I make a good gang name?
items.description: Start from the setting and tone in the Gang Name Generator, combine a striking image with the group's code and its form (crew, family, clan, syndicate), then test the name in dialogue — as a threat, a whisper, and a badge. If it survives all three, it belongs in your story.

items.title: Are the generated gang names free to use?
items.description: Yes. Names the tool invents are creative suggestions you can use, change, or discard in your fiction and games without paying anything. The tool does not run trademark checks, so search the name in quotes before commercial publication.

items.title: How do I make a gang name fit a fantasy or cyberpunk setting?
items.description: Use the World control. Fantasy names pair images with vows and orders; cyberpunk names splice tech slang with manifesto gravity; mafia names lean on dynasty and surnames. The generator rewrites its naming logic for whichever world you pick.

items.title: What is the difference between a crew, a clan, and a syndicate?
items.description: A crew is small and mobile, built on personal loyalty. A clan is an old bloodline with ancestral territory and grudges. A syndicate is sprawling and businesslike, with legitimate fronts and a cold chain of command. The Group type control changes all of this.

items.title: Does this tool generate real gang names?
items.description: No, and it is designed never to. Every name, symbol, and territory is invented fiction. The generator refuses real-world gang names, symbols, members, and structures, and it produces nothing that could serve real recruitment or intimidation.

items.title: Can I generate mafia, biker, or funny gang names?
items.description: Yes. Set World to Mafia or Outlaw biker for those registers, or turn the Tone dial to Funny for darkly comedic names. Combine a world with a tone — cyberpunk and funny — for hybrid flavors.

items.title: Is the first generation really free?
items.description: Yes. Every generation on this page is free and works without an account or sign-in — pick your controls and generate as often as you like.
